Kiri can notice the TV’s own home screen coming up and open right in its place. For that it uses Android’s accessibility service, the only way Android gives an app to know it.
When a window of %1$s comes up, Android tells Kiri which one it is, and Kiri opens if it is the home screen. It hears from no other app.
It reads nothing on the screen, does not see what you type or watch, and collects or sends no data.
Right here, with Turn off: the service leaves Android’s list, and Home opens %1$s again.
Opens the TV’s Accessibility settings, where you turn Kiri on
Kiri comes in place of %1$s whenever the Home button opens it.
